title: Thietmar of Merseburg: Waic receives a crown and a blessing
fact_summary: Thietmar, bishop of Merseburg, records in one sentence that Waic, son-in-law of the duke of the Bavarians, set up bishoprics in his kingdom and received a crown and blessing by the emperor's favour. The edition identifies Waic as Stephen, king of Hungary.

place.label: Merseburg, where Thietmar was bishop
place.note: Pinned by Claude at the city of Merseburg, Thietmar's see according to the edition's title. The pin marks where the text comes from, not where the crowning happened; the passage names no place for it.

claims.text: Thietmar writes: “By the favour and urging of the aforesaid emperor, the son-in-law of Henry, duke of the Bavarians, Waic, setting up bishops' sees in his own kingdom, received a crown and blessing” (coronam et benediccionem accepit).
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: The edition's index of names identifies Waic with Stephen: “Waic (= Stephanus) rex Pannonicus”, king of Pannonia.

sources.locator: Kurze ed., index of names, under “Waic” and “Stephanus”

claims.certainty_reason: This records what the edition's index says, read in the scanned edition linked under Sources.

claims.text: The editor's margin marks this passage as “man. D al. temp.”, and prints it in square brackets, with the name Waic in brackets of its own.
claims.certainty_reason: The marks were read in the scan. Claude takes them to mean that the passage was added to the manuscript by a different hand at another time; the edition's key to its signs has not been read to confirm this.

claims.text: The chapter before, speaking of the Polish ruler Boleslav, says he “took a wife from Hungary” (ab Ungaria), had a son by her, and sent her away.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

dating_methods.text: Thietmar gives no year for the crowning. He speaks of “the aforesaid emperor”; the chapter before dates another event to 992 “in the reign of the third Otto”.
dating_methods.certainty_reason: Read in Latin. That “the aforesaid emperor” is Otto III is Claude's reading of the context, not something the sentence states.

dating_methods.text: A 2021 genetic study, in its historical summary, says the Hungarians “founded the Hungarian Kingdom around 1000AD”. The pin's year on the timeline follows that round figure.
dating_methods.certainty_reason: A passing statement in a genetics paper, not a historical study. No source that dates the crowning itself has been read yet.

open_questions.text: In which year, and where, was the crown received? No source that gives the date has been read yet.
Thietmar credits the emperor. Who sent the crown, and what do Hungarian sources say?
Why does Thietmar call him Waic and not Stephen?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
